name: See
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain village in the Paznauntal with family-friendly slopes and a sunny village center – peaceful and relaxing.
beschreibung:
Overview

See is located at 1,056 meters above sea level at the entrance to the picturesque Paznaun valley in the Landeck district of the Tyrolean Oberland, roughly ten kilometers southwest of Landeck-Zams. As the very first village in the valley, the municipality of roughly 1,300 residents nestles across sunny alluvial fans and slopes at the northern foot of the Samnaun mountain range (including Medrigjoch at 2,270 m and Mount Furgler at 3,004 m), bordered by the rushing Trisanna river. Offering a tranquil counterpoint to the energetic resort of Ischgl further up the valley, See is celebrated as an exceptionally family-friendly, authentic alpine destination. Featuring a high-altitude ski domain extending up to 2,570 meters, an extensive lake adventure park in the village center, and deep-rooted alpine farming traditions, See offers supreme recreation across all seasons.

History

The name See (meaning lake) reflects a prehistoric geological event: a massive post-glacial rockslide dammed the Trisanna river, creating a large natural lake in the valley basin. When this barrier eventually breached, it left behind the fertile, level valley floor that forms today's village. While the upper Paznaun was settled by Romansh and Walser pioneers, lower Paznaun was originally cleared and cultivated by farmers arriving from Serfaus and Fiss across the mountains in the 13th century. Consequently, See remained ecclesiastically attached to Serfaus until 1630 and governed under Laudeck court until 1792. The settlement was first formally documented in 1433 as ze dem See in Pacznawn. The Baroque parish church of Saint Sebastian was constructed between 1758 and 1761, featuring ceiling frescoes by Johann Wörle and an ornate Madonna statue.

Getting there

See benefits from safe, year-round road connections. Drivers leave the A12 motorway or S16 Arlberg expressway at the Pians/Paznaun/Ischgl exit, following the B188 Paznaun valley road for just seven kilometers directly into See. Rail travelers arrive at the Landeck-Zams railway station, an international hub served by all ÖBB Railjet trains. Directly from the station forecourt, VVT regional bus line 260 runs every 30 to 60 minutes straight to See, taking merely 20 minutes. Holidaymakers holding the Silvretta Card Premium travel free on regional bus lines throughout the entire Paznaun valley.

Tips

During winter, the Bergbahnen See ski area offers 41 kilometers of snow-assured pistes reaching up to 2,570 meters, modern lifts such as the Furglerblick gondola, a dedicated children's snow park, and a six-kilometer natural toboggan run featuring weekly night sledging. In summer, the Badesee See adventure park provides refreshing fun with its spring-fed swimming lake, kids' splash zone, sun terraces, and sports courts. Just next to the lake, hike into the dramatic Schaller Klamm gorge along wooden walkways and rushing waterfalls. Alpine enthusiasts can hike up to the traditional Ascherhütte at 2,256 meters to sample protected Paznaun Alpine cheese, while autumn visitors can experience authentic cattle and sheep drive festivals.
